entities.summary: Presidential elections were held in Mongolia on 24 May 2009. They were contested between incumbent Nambaryn Enkhbayar, supported by the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party, and Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj, who had support of the Democratic Party and the opposition parties. Elbegdorj declared himself the victor before the count was official but based on his party's counts. Enkhbayar admitted a narrow defeat shortly after and said that he would respect the results, marking the second time an incumbent president had lost their bid for re-election - following Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat in the 1997 election.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The election marked a significant shift in Mongolian politics, as it was the second time an incumbent president had lost their bid for re-election. Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj's victory led to his appointment as Prime Minister and paved the way for a new era of democratic governance in Mongolia.
